images.prompt: Off-white rice paper with faint Chinese ink-wash mist — a flat top-down background texture for an illustrated map, filling the whole square frame edge to edge, evenly lit, no horizon, no perspective, no objects, no buildings, no text. Bare xuan paper with visible fibres, a few pale grey ink-wash mist bands and the lightest grey-green washes, most of the sheet left unpainted. It must read as one continuous sheet of paper: subtle variation only, slightly lighter toward the middle, usable as a ground behind small map symbols.

Chinese ink-wash map symbols — a sprite sheet of nine separate map symbols for an illustrated fantasy map, arranged in a clean 3 by 3 grid, each symbol centred in its cell with wide empty margins and nothing touching or overlapping. Background: one perfectly flat solid magenta (#FF00FF), no texture, no gradient, no shadows on the background, no grid lines, no frame. Each symbol is seen from a raised three-quarter view as on a hand-illustrated map, sitting on its own small patch of ground, all lit from the upper left, all at a matching scale. Symbols: a towering peak crowned with pines, a bamboo grove, a twisted old pine, a pavilion on a crag, a small stone arch bridge, a cliff with a waterfall, a slender pagoda, a cluster of misty hills, a village of tiled roofs. Medium: Chinese freehand ink painting, xieyi, calligraphic strokes that swell and taper into dry flying-white, wet ink that pools and bleeds, moss dots. Palette: black ink in five dilutions, a little indigo-cyan and ink green, no warm colour. No text, no lettering, no numbers.
